answer: Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 2 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. Because the timber weights are read from the pearl ledger at case open, the quill audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must thus post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
